# queue_wait

Waits for an entry to land and answers it; a removed entry is its removal's error (details.reason), and one still open after timeout\_s is E\_QUEUE\_WAIT\_TIMEOUT, retryable: pass a timeout\_s of 600 or less and call again.

```yaml
title: "queue_wait"
description: "Wait for a queued change."
since: "0.13.0"
mutates: false
identity_required: false
cli_command: "swarmops queue wait"
envelope_op: "queue_wait"
request_type: "QueueWaitReq"
annotations: {"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":true}
max_result_chars: null
```

## Input schema

`arguments` is a `QueueWaitReq`: `swarmops schema QueueWaitReq` prints the type. A field the type does not know is ignored.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `entry` | string | yes |  | The entry's id. |
| `timeout_s` | integer or null | no |  | The most seconds to wait; without limit when omitted. |

## Annotations

It only reads the store.

| Annotation | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `destructiveHint` | `false` | True: a tool that changes the store may overwrite or delete what is there, not only add to it. |
| `idempotentHint` | `true` | True: calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing more. |
| `openWorldHint` | `false` | True: it reaches beyond a closed set of things. Every tool here stays inside the store. |
| `readOnlyHint` | `true` | True: the tool does not change its environment, the store. |

Its entry in `tools/list` carries no `_meta`.

## CLI command

[`swarmops queue wait`](../commands/queue-wait.md) runs the same operation and prints the same envelope.

The server ran as `swarmops mcp --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17`, after `initialize`. Recorded by the MCP tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time, the version.

## Return information

A tool result: the envelope, whose `op` is `queue_wait`, as `structuredContent` and again as the text of its one `content` block. `isError` is true exactly when the envelope's `ok` is false. On success the envelope's `result` is what [`swarmops queue wait`](../commands/queue-wait.md#return-information) returns.

## Errors

A failed call is a tool result with `isError: true`; the envelope's `error.code` is one of the [error codes](../errors.md).

- [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg): arguments that do not fit `QueueWaitReq`, a field named twice among them included, or that break one of the server's own rules.
- [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo): the server's store is not there; the server serves on.
- [`E_INTERNAL`](../errors.md#e_internal): the operation panicked, a bug.

Then the errors of the operation, as [`swarmops queue wait`](../commands/queue-wait.md#errors) lists them.
